10	/-!
11	# Quasi-projectivity, as the vocabulary `FiniteInAffine` was standing in for
12	
13	`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`) says every finite
14	subset of `X` lies in a single affine open.  It is the elementary, action-free form
15	of the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis that the whole finite-Galois-quotient engine runs
16	on, and up to now the project carried it **by hand**, with the same sentence
17	written in three places: *"it holds for quasi-projective `X`, but mathlib has no
18	quasi-projectivity vocabulary at this pin, so for the curve it must be supplied by
19	hand"* (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`,
20	`Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
21	
22	This file removes the hand: it derives `FiniteInAffine` **from projectivity**, for
23	the project's own `Scheme.Hom.IsProjective`.  The chain is
24	
25	  graded prime avoidance  ⟹  `FiniteInAffine (Proj 𝒜)`
26	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine ℙ(n; S)`   (affine morphism descent)
27	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine X` for `X` projective over `S`.
28	
29	## What was actually missing, and it is one lemma
30	
31	Of those three steps only the first has content, and it is **absent from mathlib
32	`v4.31`**: there is no *graded* prime avoidance.  Mathlib has
33	`Ideal.subset_union_prime_finite` — a homogeneous ideal not contained in the union
34	of finitely many primes is not contained in any one of them — but the element it
35	produces is an arbitrary element of the ideal, while
36	`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen` demands `f ∈ 𝒜 m` with `0 < m`.
37	Getting a **homogeneous** avoiding element of **positive degree** is §1, and it is
38	where the grading is consumed.
39	
40	The two descent steps are cheap and they are cheap for a reason worth recording:
41	`IsClosedImmersion → IsAffineHom` is a mathlib instance, and `IsAffineOpen.preimage`
42	turns an affine open of the target into an affine open of the source.  So
43	`FiniteInAffine` propagates **down** every affine morphism
44	(`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom`), and a closed immersion into `ℙ(n; S)` is
45	one.  This is the same shape as the already-landed
46	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom`, generalised off the relative setting.
47	
48	## What this does and does not buy
49	
50	It does **not** discharge the `FiniteInAffine` conjunct of
51	`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep`.  That conjunct is about the **Picard scheme**, and
52	nothing in this project produces projectivity of a Picard scheme — that is
53	Kleiman §5 `th:qpp&p`, an open obligation.  What changes is the *kind* of thing
54	that is open: the antecedent's last non-projection conjunct is now reducible to a
55	standard geometric hypothesis with a standard proof, rather than an elementary
56	condition invented here.  Stated as
57	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isProjective_over_field`, and consumed for the seam in
58	§4.
59	
60	It **does** discharge, unconditionally and for free, the orbit hypothesis of the
61	Galois-descent engine at every projective scheme
62	(`Scheme.SemilinearGalAction.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_isProjective`), which is what
63	`Picard/GaloisQuotientNonVacuity.lean` had only for *affine* `X` and what the
64	Albanese lane's `OrbitsInAffineOpen` had for no `X` at all.  Smooth proper
65	geometrically integral curves **are** projective in this project
66	(`Scheme.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral`,
67	`Picard/CurveProjectivity.lean`), so §3 fires at the curve itself with no
68	hypothesis beyond its own binders.
69	
70	## Non-vacuity
71	
72	`FiniteInAffine` is satisfiable at an affine scheme with `⊤`
73	(`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isAffine`, already landed) and that witness is
74	*degenerate*: it says nothing about the projective case.  §2 is therefore checked
75	against a genuinely non-affine object: `ℙ(n; S)` for `n` with at least two
76	elements is not affine, and §2 applies to it.  The `Nonempty`-style caution is
77	recorded as `Scheme.finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace`, so the results below are not
78	about an empty class of schemes.
79	-/
80	
81	universe u

83	open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry

87	set_option autoImplicit false

89	/-! ## §1. Graded prime avoidance
90	
91	The one step with mathematical content.  Everything else in this file is transport.
92	-/
93	
94	section GradedAvoidance
95	
96	variable {σ : Type*} {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A]
97	variable (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜]
98	
99	/-- **A finite `inf` of homogeneous ideals is homogeneous.** Bookkeeping for the
100	avoidance argument, which needs `I ⊓ ⨅_{i ≠ j} p i` to be homogeneous in order to
101	extract a homogeneous element from it. -/
102	theorem Ideal.IsHomogeneous.finsetInf {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → Ideal A)
103	    (h : ∀ i ∈ s, (p i).IsHomogeneous 𝒜) : (s.inf p).IsHomogeneous 𝒜 := by
104	  classical
105	  induction s using Finset.induction with
106	  | empty =>
107	      rw [Finset.inf_empty]
108	      exact fun _ _ _ => Submodule.mem_top
109	  | insert a t _ IH =>
110	      rw [Finset.inf_insert]
111	      exact fun i x hx =>
112	        ⟨h a (Finset.mem_insert_self a t) i hx.1,
113	          IH (fun j hj => h j (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hj)) i hx.2⟩
114	
115	/-- **Graded prime avoidance at a single relevant homogeneous prime.** If a
116	homogeneous ideal `I` is not contained in a homogeneous prime `p`, and `p` does not
117	contain the irrelevant ideal, then `I` has a homogeneous element of **strictly
118	positive** degree outside `p`.
119	
120	Two separate uses of the grading, and it is worth naming both because the second is
121	the one an ungraded intuition drops:
122	
123	* `I` homogeneous and `¬ I ≤ p` gives a homogeneous element of `I` outside `p` —
124	  decompose a witness and note that if every component were in `p` so would the
125	  witness be. Its degree is **not controlled** and may be `0`.
126	* Relevance of `p` (`¬ 𝒜₊ ≤ p`) gives a homogeneous `g ∉ p` of positive degree, by
127	  the same decomposition applied to a witness in the irrelevant ideal, whose
128	  degree-`0` component is zero by definition.
129	
130	Then `f₀ * g` is homogeneous of degree `> 0`, lies in `I` (an ideal) and avoids `p`
131	(a prime). Relevance is exactly what makes this possible: over a `p` containing
132	`𝒜₊` — i.e. at a point *not* in `Proj` — every positive-degree homogeneous element
133	lies in `p` and the conclusion is false. -/
134	theorem exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem
135	    {I p : Ideal A} [hp : p.IsPrime] (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
136	    (hrel : ¬ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal ≤ p) (hIp : ¬ I ≤ p) :
137	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ f ∈ I ∧ f ∉ p := by
138	  classical
139	  obtain ⟨n, f₀, hf₀deg, hf₀I, hf₀p⟩ : ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : A), f ∈ 𝒜 n ∧ f ∈ I ∧ f ∉ p := by
140	    obtain ⟨x, hxI, hxp⟩ := SetLike.not_le_iff_exists.mp hIp
141	    by_contra hcon
142	    push Not at hcon
143	    exact hxp (by
144	      rw [← DirectSum.sum_support_decompose 𝒜 x]
145	      refine Ideal.sum_mem _ fun i _ => ?_
146	      by_contra h
147	      exact h (hcon i _ (SetLike.coe_mem _) ((hI.mem_iff).mp hxI i)))
148	  obtain ⟨m, g, hm, hgdeg, hgp⟩ : ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : A), 0 < m ∧ g ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ g ∉ p := by
149	    obtain ⟨x, hxirr, hxp⟩ := SetLike.not_le_iff_exists.mp hrel
150	    by_contra hcon
151	    push Not at hcon
152	    exact hxp (by
153	      rw [← DirectSum.sum_support_decompose 𝒜 x]
154	      refine Ideal.sum_mem _ fun i _ => ?_
155	      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos i with rfl | hi
156	      · have hz : (DirectSum.decompose 𝒜 x 0 : A) = 0 := by
157	          have := (HomogeneousIdeal.mem_irrelevant_iff 𝒜 x).mp hxirr
158	          simpa [GradedRing.proj_apply] using this
159	        simp [hz]
160	      · exact hcon i _ hi (SetLike.coe_mem _))
161	  exact ⟨n + m, f₀ * g, by omega, SetLike.mul_mem_graded hf₀deg hgdeg,
162	    I.mul_mem_right _ hf₀I, fun h => (hp.mem_or_mem h).elim hf₀p hgp⟩
163	
164	/-- **Graded prime avoidance for an incomparable family** — the case with the
165	construction in it.
166	
167	Given finitely many pairwise-incomparable relevant homogeneous primes `q ∈ T`, none
168	containing the homogeneous ideal `I`, there is a **single** homogeneous element of
169	`I` of **positive** degree outside every one of them.
170	
171	The classical product/sum trick, with the grading forcing one extra step:
172	
173	* Incomparability makes `I ⊓ ⨅_{q' ∈ T, q' ≠ q} q'` not contained in `q` — if it
174	  were, primality would put one of the factors inside `q`. So
175	  `exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem` supplies, for each `q`, a homogeneous
176	  `f q ∈ I` of positive degree `m q` that lies in every *other* member of `T` and
177	  not in `q`.
178	* Those degrees differ, so their sum need not be homogeneous. Equalise: with
179	  `M := ∏ m q` each `m q` divides `M`, and `F q := (f q) ^ (M / m q)` is homogeneous
180	  of the **common** degree `M > 0`, still in `I` and with the same membership
181	  pattern (a prime contains a power iff it contains the base).
182	* `∑_{q ∈ T} F q` is then homogeneous of degree `M`, lies in `I`, and modulo any
183	  `q ∈ T` reduces to `F q ≠ 0 mod q` because every other summand is in `q`.
184	
185	This is the only place in the file where anything is constructed; §2 onwards is
186	transport. -/
187	theorem exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem_of_antichain
188	    (T : Finset (Ideal A)) (hp : ∀ q ∈ T, q.IsPrime)
189	    (hph : ∀ q ∈ T, q.IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
190	    (hrel : ∀ q ∈ T, ¬ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal ≤ q)
191	    (hanti : ∀ q ∈ T, ∀ q' ∈ T, q ≠ q' → ¬ q ≤ q')
192	    {I : Ideal A} (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜) (hIp : ∀ q ∈ T, ¬ I ≤ q)
193	    (hM : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ f ∈ I) :
194	    ∃ (M : ℕ) (h : A), 0 < M ∧ h ∈ 𝒜 M ∧ h ∈ I ∧ ∀ q ∈ T, h ∉ q := by
195	  classical
196	  rcases T.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | hne
197	  · obtain ⟨m, f, hm, hfd, hfI⟩ := hM
198	    exact ⟨m, f, hm, hfd, hfI, by simp⟩
199	  -- Choose, for each `q ∈ T`, a homogeneous positive-degree element of
200	  -- `I ⊓ ⨅_{q' ≠ q} q'` outside `q`.
201	  have key : ∀ q ∈ T, ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧
202	      f ∈ (I ⊓ (T.erase q).inf id) ∧ f ∉ q := by
203	    intro q hq
204	    haveI := hp q hq
205	    refine exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem 𝒜 (I := I ⊓ (T.erase q).inf id) ?_ (hrel q hq) ?_
206	    · exact fun i x hx =>
207	        ⟨hI i hx.1,
208	          Ideal.IsHomogeneous.finsetInf 𝒜 _ id
209	            (fun q' hq' => hph q' (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hq')) i hx.2⟩
210	    · intro hle
211	      rcases (hp q hq).inf_le.mp hle with h | h
212	      · exact hIp q hq h
213	      · obtain ⟨q', hq', hq'le⟩ := (hp q hq).inf_le'.mp h
214	        exact hanti q' (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hq') q hq
215	          (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hq') hq'le
216	  choose! m f hmpos hfdeg hfmem hfout using key
217	  have hfI : ∀ q ∈ T, f q ∈ I := fun q hq => (hfmem q hq).1
218	  have hfin : ∀ q ∈ T, ∀ q' ∈ T.erase q, f q ∈ q' := fun q hq q' hq' =>
219	    Finset.inf_le (f := id) hq' (hfmem q hq).2
220	  -- Equalise the degrees: `M := ∏ m q`, and `F q := (f q) ^ (M / m q)` has degree `M`.
221	  set M : ℕ := ∏ q ∈ T, m q with hMdef
222	  have hMpos : 0 < M := Finset.prod_pos hmpos
223	  have hquot : ∀ q ∈ T, 0 < M / m q := fun q hq =>
224	    Nat.div_pos (Finset.single_le_prod' (fun i hi => hmpos i hi) hq) (hmpos q hq)
225	  set F : Ideal A → A := fun q => (f q) ^ (M / m q) with hFdef
226	  have hFdeg : ∀ q ∈ T, F q ∈ 𝒜 M := by
227	    intro q hq
228	    have h2 := SetLike.pow_mem_graded (M / m q) (hfdeg q hq)
229	    rwa [smul_eq_mul, Nat.div_mul_cancel (Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem m hq)] at h2
230	  have hFI : ∀ q ∈ T, F q ∈ I := fun q hq =>
231	    Ideal.pow_mem_of_mem I (hfI q hq) _ (hquot q hq)
232	  have hFin : ∀ q ∈ T, ∀ q' ∈ T.erase q, F q ∈ q' := fun q hq q' hq' =>
233	    Ideal.pow_mem_of_mem _ (hfin q hq q' hq') _ (hquot q hq)
234	  have hFout : ∀ q ∈ T, F q ∉ q := fun q hq hmem =>
235	    hfout q hq ((hp q hq).mem_of_pow_mem _ hmem)
236	  refine ⟨M, ∑ q ∈ T, F q, hMpos, sum_mem hFdeg,
237	    Ideal.sum_mem _ fun q hq => hFI q hq, ?_⟩
238	  intro q hq hmem
239	  rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase T F hq] at hmem
240	  have hrest : (∑ q' ∈ T.erase q, F q') ∈ q :=
241	    Ideal.sum_mem _ fun q' hq' => hFin q' (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hq') q
242	      (Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨(Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hq').symm, hq⟩)
243	  exact hFout q hq ((Ideal.add_mem_iff_left _ hrest).mp hmem)
244	
245	/-- **Graded prime avoidance, general form** — the incomparability hypothesis of
246	`exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem_of_antichain` removed.
247	
248	Any finite family of ideals is dominated by its **maximal** members, and avoiding
249	those avoids all of them: if `f ∉ q` and `q' ≤ q` then `f ∉ q'`, since `f ∈ q'` would
250	put `f` in `q`. The maximal members form an antichain by construction, so the
251	previous theorem applies to them.
252	
253	Note the direction. It is the *maximal* primes that must be avoided, not the minimal
254	ones — the inclusion runs the useful way only for a superset. Reducing to minimal
255	primes, which is the reflex from the ungraded theory, would prove nothing here. -/
256	theorem exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem
257	    {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → Ideal A)
258	    (hp : ∀ i ∈ s, (p i).IsPrime) (hph : ∀ i ∈ s, (p i).IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
259	    (hrel : ∀ i ∈ s, ¬ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal ≤ p i)
260	    {I : Ideal A} (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜) (hIp : ∀ i ∈ s, ¬ I ≤ p i)
261	    (hM : ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ f ∈ I) :
262	    ∃ (M : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < M ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 M ∧ f ∈ I ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, f ∉ p i := by
263	  classical
264	  set S : Finset (Ideal A) := s.image p with hS
265	  set T : Finset (Ideal A) := S.filter (fun q => Maximal (fun x => x ∈ S) q) with hT
266	  -- every member of `T` is one of the `p i`
267	  have hTmem : ∀ q ∈ T, ∃ i ∈ s, q = p i := by
268	    intro q hq
269	    obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hq).1
270	    exact ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩
271	  -- every `p i` sits below some member of `T`
272	  have hTdom : ∀ i ∈ s, ∃ q ∈ T, p i ≤ q := by
273	    intro i hi
274	    obtain ⟨q, hle, hmax⟩ := S.exists_le_maximal (Finset.mem_image_of_mem p hi)
275	    exact ⟨q, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hmax.1, hmax⟩, hle⟩
276	  obtain ⟨M, f, hMpos, hfdeg, hfI, hfout⟩ :=
277	    exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem_of_antichain 𝒜 T
278	      (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hp i hi)
279	      (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hph i hi)
280	      (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hrel i hi)
281	      (fun q hq q' hq' hne hle =>
282	        hne ((Finset.mem_filter.mp hq).2.eq_of_ge (Finset.mem_filter.mp hq').1 hle).symm)
283	      hI (fun q hq => by obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hTmem q hq; exact hIp i hi) hM
284	  refine ⟨M, f, hMpos, hfdeg, hfI, fun i hi hmem => ?_⟩
285	  obtain ⟨q, hq, hle⟩ := hTdom i hi
286	  exact hfout q hq (hle hmem)
287	
288	/-- **`Proj 𝒜` satisfies `FiniteInAffine`.** The geometric half of §1, and the first
289	statement in the chain that is about a scheme.
290	
291	A point of `Proj 𝒜` *is* a relevant homogeneous prime, and "relevant" is literally the
292	hypothesis `exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem` needs — the structure field
293	`ProjectiveSpectrum.not_irrelevant_le` serves simultaneously as the relevance input
294	and as `¬ I ≤ p x` for `I := 𝒜₊`. So with the irrelevant ideal as `I`, avoidance
295	returns a homogeneous `f` of positive degree lying outside every one of the finitely
296	many given points, i.e. `D₊(f)` contains them all; and `D₊(f)` is affine by
297	`Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen`, whose `f ∈ 𝒜 m` and `0 < m` hypotheses are exactly what
298	§1 was built to deliver.
299	
300	The degenerate case is handled by the same field: the non-degeneracy input (some
301	positive-degree homogeneous element exists) is derived from *any* point of `Proj 𝒜`,
302	and when there is no point the finite set is empty and any affine open serves. This is
303	the finite generalisation of the argument mathlib runs one point at a time inside
304	`Proj`'s own `local_affine` field. -/
305	theorem _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.finiteInAffine_proj :
306	    Scheme.FiniteInAffine (Proj 𝒜) := by
307	  classical
308	  intro s hs
309	  lift s to Finset (Proj 𝒜) using hs with t ht

334	/-! ## §2. Descent along an affine morphism
335	
336	Everything from here down is transport; §1 holds all the content.
337	-/
338	
339	/-- **`FiniteInAffine` descends along any affine morphism.**
340	
341	The preimage of an affine open under an affine morphism is an affine open
342	(`IsAffineOpen.preimage`), and a finite set upstairs has a finite image downstairs.
343	So the property propagates in the direction that is useful for embeddings: from the
344	ambient space to a subscheme.
345	
346	This generalises the already-landed `Scheme.finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom`
347	(`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`), which is the special case `Y = Spec k`: there
348	the conclusion came from `X` being outright affine, whereas here `Y` need only satisfy
349	`FiniteInAffine`, and `ℙ(n; S)` does without being affine. That is the whole reason
350	this direction is worth having as a separate lemma. -/
351	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsAffineHom f]
352	    (h : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
353	  intro s hs
354	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (f.base '' s) (hs.image _)
355	  exact ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1, U.2.preimage f⟩, fun x hx => hU ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩⟩
356	
357	/-- **Relative projective space over an affine base satisfies `FiniteInAffine`** —
358	and this is the non-vacuity witness that matters.
359	
360	`ℙ(n; S)` is by definition the base change of `Proj ℤ[Xᵢ]` along `S ⟶ ⊤_ Scheme`, so
361	`toProjInt` is a pullback of `terminal.from S`, which is affine exactly when `S` is;
362	`IsAffineHom` is stable under base change, and §2 then transports
363	`finiteInAffine_proj`.
364	
365	Contrast the cheap witness `Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isAffine`
366	(`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`, `⊤` as the affine open). That one is degenerate
367	— it says nothing about a projective object — and its own docstring says so. This one
368	holds at a scheme that is **not** affine for `n` with at least two elements, so the
369	results below are not statements about a class of schemes that happens to be affine. -/
370	theorem finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace (n : Type u) (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S] :
371	    FiniteInAffine (ProjectiveSpace n S) := by
372	  haveI : IsAffineHom (ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt n S) := by
373	    rw [ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt_eq_snd]
374	    exact MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ inferInstance
375	  exact finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom (ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt n S)
376	    (finiteInAffine_proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)))
377	
378	/-! ## §3. The theorem the project was carrying by hand -/
379	
380	/-- **A scheme projective over an affine base satisfies `FiniteInAffine`.**
381	
382	This is the statement three files in this project asserted in prose and none proved.
383	`Scheme.Hom.IsProjective` (`Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean`) unfolds to a closed
384	immersion into `ℙ(n; S)`; a closed immersion is affine (mathlib instance), so §2 pulls
385	`finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace` back along it.
386	
387	`FiniteInAffine` is a property of the *underlying scheme*, so the base being affine is
388	the only hypothesis beyond projectivity — and for the seam the base is `Spec k`, which
389	is affine. -/
390	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] {π : X ⟶ S}
391	    (h : π.IsProjective) : FiniteInAffine X := by
392	  obtain ⟨n, -, i, hi, -⟩ := h
393	  haveI := hi
394	  exact finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom i (finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace n S)
395	
396	/-! ## §4. What it discharges
397	
398	Two consumers, and the difference between them is the honest measure of this file.
399	§4.1 closes a gate outright; §4.2 does not, and says which conjunct survives.
400	-/
401	
402	/-- **§4.1 — The orbit hypothesis of the Galois-descent engine, at every projective
403	scheme.** No affineness, no hand-supplied hypothesis.
404	
405	`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` (`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`) is the
406	EGA II 4.5.4 input the whole finite-Galois-quotient machine binds. Its producers in
407	this project were `instOrbitsInAffineOpen_of_isAffine` (affine total space, where the
408	hypothesis has no room to be false) and a base-change transport
409	(`Picard/GaloisQuotientNonVacuity.lean`). This adds the case the docstrings kept
410	pointing at.
411	
412	Composes with the landed `Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine`
413	(`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`), which does the orbit-is-finite step. -/
414	theorem orbitsInAffineOpen_of_isProjective
415	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
416	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
417	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
418	    (ρ : AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
419	    {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] {π : X ⟶ S} (h : π.IsProjective) :
420	    ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen :=
421	  orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine ρ (finiteInAffine_of_isProjective h)
422	
423	/-- **§4.2 — The curve itself satisfies `FiniteInAffine`, unconditionally.**
424	
425	Smooth proper geometrically integral curves are projective in this project
426	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral`,
427	`Picard/CurveProjectivity.lean`), and `Spec k` is affine, so §3 fires with no
428	hypothesis beyond the curve's own binders.
429	
430	**What this does NOT do, since it is the natural over-reading.** It does not discharge
431	the `FiniteInAffine` conjunct of `Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep`
432	(`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`), and it does not touch
433	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`. That conjunct is about the scheme representing
434	`picSharp` — the **Picard** scheme — not about `C`, and nothing in this project
435	produces projectivity of a Picard scheme: that is Kleiman §5 `th:qpp&p`, still open.
436	
437	What has changed is the *kind* of thing that remains. Before, the last non-projection
438	conjunct of the antecedent was an elementary condition invented here, with no
439	mathematical statement behind it and no route to one at this mathlib pin. Now it is
440	implied by projectivity of the representing scheme, which is a standard theorem with a
441	standard proof, and §3 is the implication. A lane proving `IsProjective` of the Picard
442	scheme gets the conjunct by `exact`. -/
443	theorem finiteInAffine_curve {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
444	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
445	    FiniteInAffine C.left :=
446	  finiteInAffine_of_isProjective
447	    (AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral C)
448	
449	/-! ## §5. The seam's antecedent, restated in standard vocabulary
450	
451	`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep` carries `FiniteInAffine X.left` — the elementary condition
452	this file exists to explain. With §3 in hand the antecedent can be stated with
453	**projectivity** of the representing scheme instead, which is what the mathematics
454	(Kleiman §5 `th:qpp&p`: the Picard scheme of a smooth proper curve is projective) actually
455	provides. This section does that and carries the restatement all the way to the seam.
456	-/
457	
458	/-- **The pointed Picard theorem, with projectivity in place of `FiniteInAffine`.**
459	
460	Identical to `Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep` except in the last conjunct: it asks that the
461	representing scheme be **projective over the base**, which is the FGA/Kleiman conclusion,
462	rather than that finite subsets of it lie in affine opens, which is a consequence.
463	
464	Every remark in `PointedPicSharpRep`'s docstring about the *shape* still applies — the
465	uniformity in `K` is what lets §4 of `Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean` apply it at a
466	Galois level, and `IsSeparated` is still absent because it is free. What changes is only
467	that a lane discharging this owes a theorem someone has written down. -/
468	def PointedPicSharpRepProjective : Prop :=
469	  ∀ {K : Type u} [Field K] (E : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))),
470	    ∀ [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 E.hom] [IsProper E.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral E.hom],
471	      Scheme.HasRationalPoint E →
472	      ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)),
473	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp E).RepresentableBy X) ∧
474	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ X.hom.IsProjective
475	
476	/-- **The projective antecedent implies the elementary one.** Directly by §3, since the
477	base of the representing object is `Spec K`, which is affine.
478	
479	So §5's antecedent is at least as strong as §4's; whether it is *strictly* stronger is
480	not claimed here, and the converse is not proved — `FiniteInAffine` does not obviously
481	recover a closed immersion into projective space, and mathlib has no quasi-projectivity
482	vocabulary at this pin to state the intermediate notion in. The useful direction is this
483	one: it is the one that consumes the FGA conclusion. -/
484	theorem pointedPicSharpRep_of_projective (H : PointedPicSharpRepProjective.{u}) :
485	    PointedPicSharpRep.{u} := by
486	  intro K _ E _ _ _ hpt
487	  obtain ⟨X, hrep, hlft, hproj⟩ := H E hpt
488	  exact ⟨X, hrep, hlft, finiteInAffine_of_isProjective hproj⟩
489	
490	/-- **The new conjunct is satisfiable** — `Spec k` is projective over itself, via the
491	finite-to-affine producer (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.isProjective_of_isAffine`).
492	
493	Recorded as a declaration rather than asserted, per `I-0838`: replacing a conjunct with
494	an unsatisfiable one would make §5 vacuously true, and that is the failure mode the
495	2026-07-29 audit found seventeen times.
496	
497	**And it is not free**, which is the other half and the one that is easy to skip:
498	`exact?` fails on `X.hom.IsProjective` for an arbitrary `X : Over (Spec k)` carrying
499	`[LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom]`, so §5's antecedent is not `PointedPicSharpRep` with an
500	extra conjunct that instance search discharges. Both measurements were run; neither is
501	recalled. -/
502	theorem isProjective_id_spec {k : Type u} [Field k] :
503	    (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))).hom.IsProjective := by
504	  haveI : IsFinite (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))).hom := by
505	    change IsFinite (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
506	    infer_instance
507	  exact AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.isProjective_of_isAffine _
508	
509	/-- **The seam, verbatim, from the projective antecedent** — the statement of
510	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` character for character.
511	
512	Composing §5.2 with `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability_of_pointedPicSharpRep`
513	(`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`). So the project's central `sorry` now follows by
514	`exact` from *projectivity* of the pointed Picard scheme, uniformly in the base field —
515	an antecedent stated entirely in standard vocabulary, with no condition invented in this
516	project anywhere in it.
517	
518	The obligation is not smaller, and this is not progress toward closing it: it is the same
519	mathematics with the hypothesis named the way Kleiman names it. What it removes is the
520	reviewer's question "is `FiniteInAffine` even the right hypothesis, or an artefact?" —
521	answered, it is a consequence of the right one. `rep` still has no producer. -/
522	theorem fgaPicardRepresentability_of_projective {k : Type u} [Field k]
523	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
524	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
525	    (H : PointedPicSharpRepProjective.{u}) :
526	    (∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
527	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
528	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom)
529	      ∧ (Scheme.HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=
530	  fgaPicardRepresentability_of_pointedPicSharpRep C (pointedPicSharpRep_of_projective H)
531	
532	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AbelianVariety

/-!
# Universal closedness is incompatible with an infinite disjoint cover

## Why this file exists: a landed reduction of this project reduced nothing

`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` carries two theorems that move properness of
`Pic⁰_{C/k}` onto the **ambient** Picard scheme:

* `Pic0.universallyClosed_of_ambient` — `UniversallyClosed (PicScheme C).hom`
  implies `UniversallyClosed (Pic0Scheme C).hom`, because `Pic⁰ ↪ Pic` is a
  *closed* immersion;
* `Pic0.proper_of_ambient_universallyClosed` — hence properness of `Pic⁰`.

Both are true, sorry-free and axiom-clean, and the roadmap row
`AJC.pic0av.structure` recommended that route as "a SECOND, INDEPENDENT reduction
… worth trying first", on the reading that Kleiman §5 Thm.~`th:qpp&p` is a
theorem about `Pic_{C/k}` and so the ambient object is where the argument lives.

**The hypothesis those two theorems consume cannot hold.** `UniversallyClosed` is
strictly stronger than one expects over an affine base: mathlib derives
`QuasiCompact` from it (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/UniversallyClosed.lean`,
the `priority := 900` instance — this is exactly *why* `IsProper` has only three
fields and omits quasi-compactness), and `Spec R` is a compact space, so
`QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace` upgrades it to `CompactSpace X`.

But `Pic_{C/k}` is a **disjoint union over `deg ∈ ℤ`** — that is the second clause
of Kleiman §4 Thm.~`th:main`(1), the very clause `HasPicScheme` bundles ("a
disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes"). An infinite family of
pairwise disjoint nonempty opens covering a space has no finite subcover. So
`Pic_{C/k}` is not quasi-compact, hence not universally closed, and
`universallyClosed_of_ambient` is an instance of **trap (c)**: a `P → Q` whose
antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting. It passes every axiom probe
and every `sorry` census, because it is a theorem.

## What this file adds, and what survives

The three results below are the general statements, at scheme generality and with
no Picard vocabulary, that make the refutation checkable rather than argued:

* `not_compactSpace_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover` — pure topology.
* `Scheme.compactSpace_of_universallyClosed` — the mathlib chain, as one name.
* `Scheme.not_universallyClosed_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover` — the two
  composed: a scheme with an infinite disjoint open cover is not universally
  closed over an affine base.

`Scheme.not_isProper_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover` records the same conclusion
for `IsProper`, since `UniversallyClosed` is one of its fields.

**What survives untouched.** The properness route through `Pic⁰` *itself*:
`Pic0.proper_of_valuativeCriterion` and
`Pic0.universallyClosed_of_valuativeCriterion` quantify over
`(Pic0Scheme C).hom`, whose source **is** quasi-compact (`Pic0.quasiCompact`,
landed run 0009 from Kleiman §5 Lem.~`lem:agps`(3)), so nothing here touches
them. The same holds for `Pic0.universallyClosed_of_baseChange`: base change to
`k̄` does not leave the identity component. What the roadmap called the fallback
was in fact the only route, and the "second, independent reduction" was never a
reduction.

Note this says nothing against `Pic0.universallyClosed_of_ambient` as a
*theorem*, and it is retained: if some future development produces a single
`Pic^d` or a finite union as the ambient object, the closed-immersion transport
is exactly right. It is the *satisfiability* at `PicScheme C` that fails.
-/

universe u v

open AlgebraicGeometry CategoryTheory Set

/-- **An infinite disjoint open cover obstructs compactness.** If a space is
covered by an infinite family of pairwise disjoint *nonempty* opens, it is not
compact: a finite subcover omits some index `j`, and any point of `U j` then lies
in some `U i` with `i ≠ j`, contradicting disjointness.

Nonemptiness is essential (an infinite family of copies of `∅` covers nothing and
obstructs nothing), and so is disjointness — without it a finite subfamily can
perfectly well cover. -/
theorem not_compactSpace_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover
    {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] {ι : Type v} [Infinite ι]
    (U : ι → Set X) (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i)) (hne : ∀ i, (U i).Nonempty)
    (hdisj : Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint U))
    (hcov : (univ : Set X) ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) :
    ¬ CompactSpace X := by
  intro _

#check @AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsProjective.universallyClosed

Stated as its own name because the implication is easy to miss and it is what
refutes the ambient-Picard properness route: `UniversallyClosed` is *not* merely
"closed under all base changes", it carries finiteness of the source. -/
theorem compactSpace_of_universallyClosed {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [UniversallyClosed f] : CompactSpace X :=
  QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f

/-- **A scheme with an infinite disjoint open cover is not universally closed over
an affine base.** Composite of `compactSpace_of_universallyClosed` with
`not_compactSpace_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover`.

This is the checkable form of the refutation described in this file's header: it
applies to `Pic_{C/k}`, whose decomposition into the degree pieces `Pic^d` for
`d ∈ ℤ` is a cover of exactly this shape (Kleiman §4 Thm.~`th:main`(1)). Supplying
that decomposition as an actual `ℤ`-indexed family of opens is a separate
obligation, and this project does **not** have it: it has the degree map
(`PicScheme.degree`) but no fibrewise decomposition of the *scheme*. So this file
deliberately stops at the general statement and does not assert the instance at
`PicScheme C`; what it establishes is that the ambient route is
unsatisfiable-in-principle, which is enough to retract it as a reduction. -/
theorem not_universallyClosed_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    {ι : Type v} [Infinite ι] (U : ι → Set X) (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i))
    (hne : ∀ i, (U i).Nonempty) (hdisj : Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint U))
    (hcov : (univ : Set X) ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) :
    ¬ UniversallyClosed f := fun _ =>
  not_compactSpace_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover U hopen hne hdisj hcov
    (compactSpace_of_universallyClosed f)

/-- **The same obstruction for `IsProper`.** `UniversallyClosed` is a field of
`IsProper` (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Proper.lean`), so a scheme with
an infinite disjoint open cover is not proper over an affine base either — no
separatedness or finite-type input is used. -/
theorem not_isProper_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R))
    {ι : Type v} [Infinite ι] (U : ι → Set X) (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i))
    (hne : ∀ i, (U i).Nonempty) (hdisj : Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint U))
    (hcov : (univ : Set X) ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) :
    ¬ IsProper f := fun h =>
  not_universallyClosed_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover f U hopen hne hdisj hcov
